title: Horror Frames
summary:
Four horror directions with interchangeable-looking **heads, cores, arms, and leg assemblies**: skeletal **Ossuary**, coffin-armored **Pallbearer**, uncanny **Marionette**, and insect-like **Brood**. This round explores detailed concept art beyond the earlier low-poly style.

Visible neck collars, shoulder docks and waist bearings keep the parts readable. Their exact dimensions would be established in a later parts study. The separate Shared Hand study remains the reference for future hand geometry.

**My picks:** Marionette for uncanny horror; Ossuary for a clear skeletal identity. All four await your selection. Click an image to enlarge or download it; expand **Prompt** to see how it was made.

[Design notes](assets/horror-round-03/review.md) · [Saved prompt set](sources/horror-round-03-prompts.json)

items.title: A · Ossuary
items.body:
**Skeletal machinery · medium frame**

Pale rib-like chest armor wraps a sealed dark core. Recessed optics and a slotted face grille suggest a death mask; narrow exposed limbs make the machine feel stripped down.

**Swappable parts:** compact sensor head on a neck collar, shoulder-mounted arm assemblies, and a separate pelvis/leg chassis below the waist bearing. The rib cage belongs entirely to the torso module.

**Mix-and-match idea:** put this head and ribbed core on Brood's reverse-jointed legs.

**Review:** the head, torso, arms and legs are visibly separate; both feet and hands are in frame. Ready for your review.

[Download image](assets/horror-round-03/h03-a-ossuary-v001.png)
items.alt: Ossuary: pale rib-armored skeletal mech with a death-mask sensor head, exposed circular joints and separate limb assemblies.
items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original horror mech concept illustration for the Mech Lab design gallery.
Primary request: Invent one frightening, pilotable industrial combat mech. The horror must come from its mechanical design, silhouette and material choices. It must still read as an assembled, modular war machine whose head, torso/core, complete left and right arm assemblies, and pelvis/leg chassis could be removed and swapped onto other mechs. A substantial enclosed torso houses a pilot; no human-scale android or suit of armor.
Modular construction: clearly visible short standardized circular neck collar below the head; exposed round shoulder docking hubs separated from the torso by dark gaps; a clean waist coupling ring separating torso and pelvis; separate hip and knee mechanisms. Armor terminates before each interface. All external hoses stay within their individual module, never spanning a removable seam. All modules share practical machined-metal mounting language. Two complete arms, two complete legs. Compact mechanical hands with four articulated fingers plus an opposing thumb, a broad palm and visible wrist flange; both hands empty and visible. Horror details stay on replaceable armor, not fused across joints.
Style/medium: high-detail professional game concept painting with convincing hard-surface engineering, fine material work, crisp large forms and selective painterly edges. Smooth and curved armor is welcome; no low-poly restriction. Original industrial sci-fi design, no franchise logos or copied characters.
Composition/framing: one complete assembled mech only, full body head to feet with generous safe margins, portrait 2:3 canvas, near-front three-quarter view (about 20 degrees), both arms slightly away from torso so every major module reads. Eye-level perspective around chest height without extreme foreshortening. The entire silhouette and both feet visible. Plain warm light-gray studio background, subtle floor shadow; enough neutral fill light to read all joints and dark surfaces. An unsettling object under inspection, not a cinematic scene obscured by smoke.
Avoid: cropped extremities, extra limbs, gore, human remains, organic flesh, magical energy, fantasy plate-armor costume, capes, dangling chains or cables hiding modules, giant handheld weapons, labels, text, inset diagrams, watermark.
Direction A — OSSUARY: mortuary / skeletal machine horror. A tall, predatory medium-weight biped with a wedge-shaped death-mask sensor head: deep black paired rectangular optical cavities and a vertical slotted metal mouth grille, no literal bone or human skull. Its big enclosed reactor chest is protected by six thick curved pale ceramic rib-like armor beams, arranged as three opposing pairs over a sealed dark central pilot capsule. The cavity between ribs is deep charcoal, with one very subdued amber maintenance light. Slender lower waist, strong long thighs, narrow shins with offset exposed pistons and broad split-toe machine feet. Long pale forearm shells have an ulna-like longitudinal slit showing dark metal inside. Shoulder modules are compact curved wedges, not giant pauldrons. Bone-white aged ceramic, charcoal structural metal, heat-tinted steel joints, delicate grime in recesses; no blood. Read as excavated industrial anatomy made entirely of machinery. Pronounced negative spaces between chest ribs, compact head and narrow waist give the dread. Keep the silhouette recognizably a combat vehicle with a large torso rather than a human skeleton.

items.title: B · Pallbearer
items.body:
**Burial-vault machinery · heavy frame**

A coffin-shaped chest hatch, external locking bars and enormous planted feet turn a sealed industrial vehicle into a walking tomb. Blackened steel, bronze latches and rust-red wear carry the mood.

**Swappable parts:** the coffin is the core casing; its small slit-optic head, heavy arms and broad leg chassis meet exposed circular connections. No decorative straps bridge the module seams.

**Mix-and-match idea:** combine its massive core and arms with Marionette's blank sensor mask.

**Review:** strong weight contrast against the other three; neck, shoulder and waist interfaces remain readable. Ready for your review.

[Download image](assets/horror-round-03/h03-b-pallbearer-v001.png)
items.alt: Pallbearer: broad blackened-steel mech with a coffin-shaped locked chest, small red sensor slit and massive armored legs.

Direction B — PALLBEARER: burial-vault / crushing industrial horror. A very broad, low, massively heavy biped, with a huge upright coffin-shaped torso armor casing, a flat tapering chest slab reinforced by thick external locking bars and recessed hatch latches. The torso is wider than it is tall and visibly houses a pilot; the coffin motif comes from six-sided silhouette and lid construction. A small blunt sensor head with an extremely narrow dull red horizontal optical slit sits on a visible neck ring above the slab, not embedded in the chest. Massive squared shoulder pods, deep rectangular forearm housings, compact exposed mechanical hands. Short powerful legs on widely spaced hip pivots, large knee actuators, armored shins and enormous flat industrial feet. Heavy bolted blackened steel, oxidized gunmetal, sparse rust-red seams and dark bronze latch accents. Controlled edge wear. The chest's black gasket resembles a sealed tomb door. No skulls, bones, spikes or religious symbols: sheer funerary mass, sealed machinery and relentless pressure create horror. Keep both shoulder docking rings and waist rotation bearing visible despite the heavy armor.

items.title: C · Marionette
items.body:
**Uncanny surgical machine · tall light frame**

A blank enamel sensor mask, tilted head, long hanging arms and elongated shins suggest a jointed puppet. Faded mint paint and cracked ivory surfaces give it an abandoned medical-machine character.

**Swappable parts:** the mask is an independent head, the chest is a sealed shell, and the long arms end at distinct shoulder docks. Round wrist and waist fittings continue the shared assembly language.

**Mix-and-match idea:** use the blank head on Pallbearer for an unsettling contrast between a quiet face and a massive body.

**Review:** the most uncanny direction without relying on skull imagery. Full silhouette is visible; hand details are conceptual, not a replacement for the separate Shared Hand study. Ready for your review.

[Download image](assets/horror-round-03/h03-c-marionette-v001.png)
items.alt: Marionette: tall ivory-and-mint mech with a blank tilted mask, elongated arms and shins, and distinct shoulder and waist couplings.

Direction C — MARIONETTE: uncanny puppet / abandoned surgical-machine horror. A very tall, unnervingly narrow biped with elongated mechanical forearms and shins, but a substantial sealed pilot capsule torso. Smooth dirty ivory enamel shells cover a dark articulated machine frame. The head is a small blank oval porcelain-like sensor mask with no eyes, nose or mouth, just one narrow offset vertical optical incision emitting a tiny warm amber line. The mask mounts onto a clearly visible short neck docking collar, slightly tilted about ten degrees. High circular shoulder docks, very narrow sharply tapered shoulder armor, round elbow hinges and ringed knee actuators echo a jointed doll without human skin. The torso has two clean curved chest shell halves meeting at a thin dark center seam, a slight forward hunch, and an exposed circular waist bearing. Arms hang almost to the knees, wrists and compact five-digit mechanical hands remain practical modules. Legs have long straight shin casings, narrow knee gaps and flat stable machine feet. Small strips of faded surgical mint paint, off-white chipped enamel, dark graphite links and brushed steel. The calm near-symmetry, blank face, long proportions and quiet awkward stance make it threatening. No puppet strings, cloth, exposed flesh, smile, horns or spikes. Keep it a large piloted machine rather than a person or mannequin.

items.title: D · Brood
items.body:
**Insect machine · reverse-jointed frame**

Layered green carapace armor, clustered sensor lenses and bent legs create an ambush-predator silhouette. The shell stays visibly manufactured, with brass hardware and ribbed vents.

**Swappable parts:** a separate sensor head, two conventional arm modules and a pelvis with paired reverse-jointed legs. The neck, shoulders and waist use the same visible collar-and-gap language as the other concepts.

**Mix-and-match idea:** use the leg chassis beneath Ossuary's ribbed core while retaining a compact common hand design.

**Review:** v002 gives the outer elbow and full silhouette more room. The carapace, palette and overall pose remain consistent with v001; small generated details can vary. Ready for your review.

[Download image](assets/horror-round-03/h03-d-brood-v002.png)
items.alt: Brood: green insect-like mech with clustered sensor lenses, layered carapace armor and two reverse-jointed legs; full silhouette visible.

Direction D — BROOD: insect / infestation horror expressed through manufactured machinery. A crouched broad-shouldered medium-heavy biped with exactly TWO reverse-jointed legs and TWO arms. A compact separate angular insect-like sensor head carries a cluster of six tiny green glass lenses in a blunt metal mask. No literal insect mouth or organic eyes. The enclosed pilot torso is a squat layered beetle-carapace shell with two overlapping curved dark green armor plates; clearly manufactured segmented shell panels, seams, fasteners and ventilation slots. Rounded shoulder shells are independent modules on exposed standardized circular docking hubs. Thick angular forearms end in ordinary compact mechanical five-digit hands with visible wrist collars, NOT insect claws or scythes. Lower body is a detachable pelvis-and-two-leg chassis with powerful bent digitigrade legs: large exposed hip rings, elevated heels, elongated backward lower-leg segments and wide three-pronged metal feet. The silhouette leans forward like a patient ambush predator but remains stable and mechanically plausible. Oily midnight green ceramic armor, dull brass edge hardware, black steel understructure and very restrained sickly green sensor glints. Short nested ribbed vent banks suggest egg chambers without actual eggs or living tissue. No wings, extra appendages, tentacles, swarm, biological growth or haze. Neck, shoulder and waist exchange interfaces must be obvious against the carapace.

---
Framing revision v002 (input: h03-d-brood-v001.png):
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the edit target: the existing Brood horror mech concept. Preserve this exact mech design, pose, proportions, every armor plate and joint, colors, materials, six green sensor lenses, hands, reverse-jointed legs, lighting and plain gray-beige studio background.
Change ONLY the framing: pull the camera back slightly (about 12 percent) so the entire mech is comfortably inside the portrait image. Reconstruct the tiny cropped outer edge of the elbow on the image's left using its existing circular mechanical shape. Add clean matching background around the complete silhouette, with at least 6 percent image-width clearance at the left and right extremities and clear space above the head and below the feet. Keep a portrait 2:3 composition and the same near-front three-quarter view. No redesign, no new objects, no labels, no text. This is a framing correction for a concept gallery.

Preserved first take. The outer elbow on the image's left touches the crop, so **v002 above is the preferred presentation**. The original image and generation prompt remain available for comparison.
